p:cNvPr.descr: Some structural examples of cholesterol-derived steroids. Beginning at the top left, the first steroid is testosterone. It consists of 3 6-sided ring structures and one 5-sided ring structure. The leftmost ring structure double bonds down and left to O, and has a double bond between two carbons at the bottom right. Across from the O, the ring bonds to a second 6-sided ring to the right. Between the two is an upward solid wedged bond. The top carbon in the second ring dashed wedge bonds down to H. The second ring is bonded up and to the right to a third ring. Its bottom carbon solid wedge bonds up to H. To the right of the third ring is a 5-sided ring, with the tip pointed up. Between the two there is an upward solid wedge bond above, a dashed wedge bond to H below, and a solid wedge bonded OH above from the top carbon of the 5-sided ring. To the right is the structure of cortisol (labeled below). The leftmost ring structure double bonds down and left to O, and has a double bond between two carbons at the bottom right. Across from the O, the ring bonds to a second 6-sided ring to the right. Between the two is an upward solid wedged bond. The top carbon in the second ring dashed wedge bonds down to H. The second ring is bonded up and to the right to a third ring. Its bottom carbon solid wedge bonds up to H. To the right of the third ring is a 5-sided ring, with the tip pointed up. Between the two there is an upward solid wedge bond above, which double bonds left to O, and bonds right to C, which bonds down and right to OH. There is a dashed wedge OH bonded to the right. There is a dashed wedge bond to H below, and a solid wedge bonded OH above from the top carbon of the 5-sided ring. To the right is prednisone (labeled below). The leftmost ring structure double bonds down and left to O, and has a double bond between two carbons at the bottom right. Across from the O, the ring bonds to a second 6-sided ring to the right. Between the two is an upward solid wedged bond. The top carbon in the second ring dashed wedge bonds down to H. The second ring is bonded up and to the right to a third ring. Its bottom carbon solid wedge bonds up to H, and it double bonds on the left to O. To the right of the third ring is a 5-sided ring, with the tip pointed up. Between the two there is an upward solid wedge bond above, which double bonds left to O, and bonds right to C, which bonds down and right to OH. There is a dashed wedge OH bonded to the right. There is a dashed wedge bond to H below, and a solid wedge bonded OH above from the top carbon of the 5-sided ring. In the next row, on the far left, is beta-estradiol, labeled below. The leftmost benzene ring bonds down and left to OH, and has a double bond between two carbons at the bottom right. Across from the O, the ring bonds to a second 6-sided ring to the right. The top carbon in the second ring dashed wedge bonds down to H. The second ring is bonded up and to the right to a third ring. Its bottom carbon solid wedge bonds up to H. To the right of the third ring is a 5-sided ring, with the tip pointed up. There is a dashed wedge OH bonded above. To the right of the beta-estradiol is aldosterone, labeled below. The leftmost ring double bonds down and left to O, and has a double bond between two of its carbons to the bottom right. The ring bonds right to another 6-sided ring, with a solid wedged bond above where the rings bond. The top carbon in the ring dashed wedge bonds down to H. The ring bonds up and right to a third 6-sided ring, which solid wedge bonds up and left to OH, and the bottom carbon solid wedge bonds up to H, inside the ring. Bonded to the right of this ring is a 5-sided ring. On top, between the 2 rings, is a solid wedge bond that double bonds to O; on the bottom is a dashed wedge bonded to H. The tip of the 5-sided ring bonds up to C, which double bonds left to O and bonds up and right to C, which bonds right to OH. To the right is prednisolone, labeled below. The leftmost ring double bonds down and left to O, and has a double bond between two of its carbons to the bottom right. The ring bonds right to another 6-sided ring, with a solid wedged bond above where the rings bond. The top carbon in the ring dashed wedge bonds down to H. The ring bonds up and right to a third 6-sided ring, which solid wedge bonds up and left to OH, and the bottom carbon solid wedge bonds up to H, inside the ring. Bonded to the right of this ring is a 5-sided ring, which is tilted right. On top, between the 2 rings, is a solid wedge bond; on the bottom is a dashed wedge bonded to H. The tip of the 5-sided ring dashed wedge bonds up to OH, then right to C which double bonds up to O and right to C, which bonds right to OH. Finally, at the bottom, there is brassinolide (a brassinosteroid) (labeled below). Its leftmost 6-carbon ring structure has 2 dashed wedge bonds left to OH, which are separated by a carbon on the ring. The ring to the right has an incorporated O at the bottom right. It also double bonds down and left to O; the bond between the two has a down & left dashed wedge bond to H. The top of the bond between the rings has a solid wedge bond pointing upward; the tip of the ring has a dashed wedge bond down to H. This ring is bound up & right to a third 6-sided ring, whose bottom top solid wedge bonds up to H. This ring bonds right to a 5-sided ring, and the top of the bond has an upward solid wedge bond. The 5-sided ring's tip dashed wedge bonds up and right to H, and up to C, which dashed wedge bonds up and left to C, then solid wedge bonds up to H, then bonds right to C, which solid wedge bonds up to OH, then bonds down and right to C, which solid wedge bonds down to OH and right to C, which solid wedge bonds up to C and right to C, which then splits into a Y-shape, where Cs end the molecule.
